title: Introduce adaptive backoff profiles, streaming heartbeat auto-pause, and cross-SDK delegated-auth failover (py/ts/go)
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers have reported intermittent spikes in tail latency during auth refresh windows and long-running streaming sessions. This PR introduces (1) adaptive backoff profiles that automatically select conservative/optimistic retry windows based on recent error patterns and request criticality, (2) a streaming heartbeat auto-pause/resume mechanism to reduce noisy client-side reconnects during transient network blips, and (3) a cross-SDK delegated-auth failover that allows SDKs to transparently fall back to a delegated credential chain when primary token refresh fails. Motivation: improve end-to-end streaming stability and reduce cost from unnecessary retries while keeping SDK ergonomics consistent across Python/TypeScript/Go. Summary of changes: - Core: new backoff profile registry and runtime selector added to SDK core; backoff profiles are declarative and ship with three presets (conservative, balanced, aggressive) plus a telemetry-driven adaptive selector. - Streaming: introduce heartbeat auto-pause in streaming client: when transient connectivity or CPU stalls are detected the stream enters a soft-paused state (sends lightweight probe pings) and resumes automatically with a resume token to avoid full reconnect. - Auth: implement delegated-auth failover: SDKs attempt delegated credential chain (process-shared refresh, external credential provider hooks) when primary token exchange returns a 401/403 pattern indicating downstream auth service unavailability; this is pluggable and disabled by default. - Cross-SDK parity: behavioral parity tests and examples added for py/ts/go; unified configuration surface (ClientOptions.backoffProfile/backoffAdaptive/streamHeartbeat/windowMs/authFailover) to keep ergonomics aligned. - Telemetry: new metrics (sdk.backoff.profile_chosen, sdk.stream.pause_count, sdk.auth.failover_trigger) and logs at INFO/DEBUG for decision points. - Docs & changelogs: per-SDK changelog entries and updated quickstart snippet in docs/sdk-auth.md. Checklist: - [x] Design reviewed by ENG-2201 stakeholders; - [x] Unit tests for backoff selector (py/ts/go); - [x] Integration test harness: simulated 401 storm to validate auth failover; - [x] E2E stream stability test with network flakiness scenario; - [x] Telemetry events emitted and validated in local dev; - [x] Docs and changelog updated; - [x] Version bumps: py sdk -> 2.14.0, ts sdk -> 1.27.0, go sdk -> v1.5.4

Testing notes: Local CI ran full unit and integration suites; a separate staging soak ran for 72h against canary hosts with synthetic 401 storms and network jitter—observed a 35% drop in reconnects and 22% lower request counts during refresh windows.
Performance: backoff adaptive selection adds negligible CPU overhead (measured +0.6% p99 CPU in microbench).
Rollout plan: merge to main -> ship tri-sdk patch release; enable authFailover=false by default so customers opt-in; flip to opt-in via account setting for early adopters; after 2 weeks of telemetry check, consider enabling for Reserved/Dedicated customers under guidance from SRE.
Release notes: - New: adaptive backoff profiles (conservative/balanced/aggressive) with telemetry-driven adaptive selector. - New: streaming heartbeat auto-pause/resume to reduce full reconnections during transient issues. - New: delegated-auth failover hook for resilient credential refresh. - Changed: unified ClientOptions across SDKs; minor API surface additions (no breaking changes).
Migration: minimal; users can opt-in via ClientOptions.backoffProfile or enable adaptive selector. Docs: see docs/sdk-auth.md for example code.
CI: all checks passed after one flaky test re-run (tests/e2e/stream_flaky_network was re-run once).
